event.summary: Serena and Venus Williams made their return to the US Open women's doubles after four years but were eliminated in a closely contested first-round match. The sisters lost in a match tiebreaker, marking a dramatic end to their tournament run.

timeline.title: Alexander Zverev Claims US Open Title Over Ben Shelton
timeline.summary: Alexander Zverev of Germany won the US Open final, defeating American Ben Shelton. This victory marks Zverev's second Grand Slam title of 2026, following his earlier win at the French Open. Shelton was aiming to become the first Black man to win the men's championship since Arthur Ashe in 1968 and the first American man to win since Andy Roddick in 2003.
key_facts: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in the US Open final.

event_overview.title: About US Open
event_overview.subject: US Open
event_overview.summary: The US Open is the United States’ annual Grand Slam tennis tournament, held in New York and organized by the United States Tennis Association (USTA). It is the final Grand Slam of the tennis calendar and stages professional competition across singles, doubles, mixed doubles, wheelchair and junior events.

facts.label: 2026 dates
facts.value: The 2026 US Open ran from August 23 through September 13, 2026; main-draw singles began August 30.

facts.label: Venue
facts.value: The tournament is played at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows, New York.

facts.label: Organizer and status
facts.value: The USTA owns and organizes the US Open; it is one of tennis’s four Grand Slam tournaments, alongside the Australian Open, Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

facts.label: Competition format
facts.value: The event is a hard-court tournament and includes men’s and women’s singles and doubles, mixed doubles, wheelchair competitions and junior events.

facts.label: Rules and governance
facts.value: Grand Slam entry is subject to Grand Slam rules, regulations and code of conduct; the four major tournaments share governance on competition matters through Grand Slam Tennis.
